# Recap: the linear model

**Log fold change.** $\log_2 B-\log_2 A=\log_2\frac{B}{A}=\log_2 FC_{B/A}$; a difference of 1 on the $\log_2$ scale $\leftrightarrow$ $FC=2$.

**Model.** $y_i=\mathbf x_i^T\boldsymbol\beta+\epsilon_i$, $\epsilon_i$ i.i.d. $N(0,\sigma^2)$; matrix form $\mathbf Y=\mathbf X\boldsymbol\beta+\boldsymbol\epsilon$, $p$ = number of parameters.

**Least squares.** $\hat{\boldsymbol\beta}=(\mathbf X^T\mathbf X)^{-1}\mathbf X^T\mathbf Y$; $\hat{\mathbf Y}=\mathbf X\hat{\boldsymbol\beta}=\mathbf H\mathbf Y$, hat matrix $\mathbf H=\mathbf X(\mathbf X^T\mathbf X)^{-1}\mathbf X^T$ (projection on the column space of $\mathbf X$); leverage $h_{ii}$.

**Residual variance.** $\hat\sigma^2=\text{MSE}=\dfrac{\sum_i e_i^2}{n-p}$, $df=n-p$.

**Variance of the estimators.** $\boldsymbol\Sigma_{\hat{\boldsymbol\beta}}=(\mathbf X^T\mathbf X)^{-1}\sigma^2$.

**Contrast.** $H_0:\mathbf L^T\boldsymbol\beta=0$; $\text{var}_{\mathbf L^T\hat{\boldsymbol\beta}}=\mathbf L^T\boldsymbol\Sigma_{\hat{\boldsymbol\beta}}\mathbf L$; $T=\dfrac{\mathbf L^T\hat{\boldsymbol\beta}}{\text{SE}_{\mathbf L^T\hat{\boldsymbol\beta}}}\sim t_{n-p}$ under $H_0$.

**Two groups.** $\log_2\widehat{FC}=\bar y_{1}-\bar y_{2}$; $\text{se}_{\log_2\widehat{FC}}=\text{SD}\sqrt{\frac1{n_1}+\frac1{n_2}}$; $T=\dfrac{\log_2\widehat{FC}}{\text{se}_{\log_2\widehat{FC}}}=\dfrac{\widehat{\text{signal}}}{\widehat{\text{noise}}}$. Dummy coding: $\mu_1=\beta_0$, $\mu_2=\beta_0+\beta_1$, $\log_2 FC=\beta_1$.

# I. Proteomics: data processing

**Normalisation.** $y^\text{norm}_{ip}=y_{ip}-nf_i$, with $y_{ip}$ the $\log_2$ intensity of precursor $p$ in sample $i$. Median of ratios: pseudo-reference $\bar y_{\cdot p}$ (row mean of $\log_2$ intensities = $\log_2$ geometric mean); $nf_i=\text{median}_p\,(y_{ip}-\bar y_{\cdot p})$.

**Summarisation (maxLFQ).** Pairwise ratios $r_{ij}=\text{median}_s(y_{sj}-y_{si})$ over the shared precursors $s$; protein summaries minimise $\sum_i\sum_j(y^\text{prot}_j-y^\text{prot}_i-r_{ij})^2$.

**Summarisation (robust regression / median polish).** $y_{ip}=\beta^\text{pre}_p+\beta^\text{samp}_i+\epsilon_{ip}$; the summary of sample $i$ is $\hat\beta^\text{samp}_i$.

**Protein-level model.** $y_i=\mathbf x_i^T\boldsymbol\beta+\epsilon_i$, $\epsilon_i\sim N(0,\sigma^2)$, one model per protein.

# I. Proteomics: statistical inference

**Multiple testing.** $m$ tests; $\text{FWER}=\text{P}[FP\ge1]$. Bonferroni: $\alpha_\text{adj}=\alpha/m$ or $p_\text{adj}=\min(p\times m,1)$.

**FDR.** $\text{FDP}=\dfrac{FP}{R}$; $\text{FDR}=\text{E}\left[\frac{FP}{R}\right]=\text{E}[\text{FDP}]$.

**Benjamini--Hochberg.** Ordered p-values $p_{(1)}\le\ldots\le p_{(m)}$; reject $H_{0(1)},\ldots,H_{0(k)}$ for the largest $k$ with $p_{(k)}\le k\alpha/m$. Adjusted p-value: $\tilde p_{(i)}=\min\left[\min_{j=i,\ldots,m}\left(mp_{(j)}/j\right),1\right]$.

**Bayes.** posterior $=\dfrac{\text{prior}\times\text{likelihood}}{\text{marginal}}$: $g(\boldsymbol\theta\mid\mathbf Y)=\dfrac{f(\mathbf Y\mid\boldsymbol\theta)g(\boldsymbol\theta)}{\int f(\mathbf Y\mid\boldsymbol\theta)g(\boldsymbol\theta)d\boldsymbol\theta}$.

**limma: empirical Bayes.** Prior $\frac1{\sigma_p^2}\sim\frac1{s_0^2}\frac{\chi^2_{d_0}}{d_0}$; data $s_p^2\sim\sigma_p^2\frac{\chi^2_{d_p}}{d_p}$. Moderated variance $\tilde s_p^2=\text{E}[\sigma_p^2\mid s_p^2]=\dfrac{d_0s_0^2+d_ps_p^2}{d_0+d_p}$ (shrinkage towards $s_0^2$).

**Moderated t-test.** $\tilde T_p=\dfrac{\mathbf L^T\hat{\boldsymbol\beta}_p}{\sqrt{\mathbf L^T(\mathbf X^T\mathbf W\mathbf X)^{-1}\mathbf L\,\tilde s_p^2}}\sim t_{d_0+d_p}$ under $H_0$.

**Robust regression (M-estimation).** Least squares minimises $\sum_i(y_i-\mathbf x_i^T\boldsymbol\beta)^2$; M-estimation minimises $\sum_i\rho\left(\frac{y_i-\mathbf x_i^T\boldsymbol\beta}{\sigma}\right)$, i.e. solves $\sum_i\Psi(u_i)\mathbf x_i=\mathbf 0$ with $u_i=\frac{y_i-\mathbf x_i^T\boldsymbol\beta}{\sigma}$ and $\Psi=\rho'$. With weights $w(u_i)=\Psi(u_i)/u_i$: $\sum_iw(u_i)u_i\mathbf x_i=\mathbf 0$, solved by iteratively reweighted least squares, minimising $\sum_iw(u_i^{(k-1)})(u_i^{(k)})^2$. Huber: $w(u)=\min(1,k/|u|)$, $k=1.345$.

# I. Experimental design and blocking

**Sources of variability.** $\sigma^2=\sigma^2_\text{bio}+\sigma^2_\text{lab}+\sigma^2_\text{extraction}+\sigma^2_\text{run}+\ldots$

**Randomised complete block design.** Each block (e.g. mouse) contains all treatments; model $\sim\text{treatment}+\text{block}$. Treatment effects are estimated within blocks: the block-to-block variability cancels.

**Paired / blocked comparison.** Mouse $b_m\sim N(0,\sigma^2_b)$, $m$ mice: $\text{var}[\bar y_\text{reg}-\bar y_\text{con}]=\dfrac{2\sigma^2_\epsilon}{m}$ when both cell types come from the same mice, versus $\dfrac{2(\sigma^2_b+\sigma^2_\epsilon)}{m}$ when they come from different mice.

# I. Linear mixed models

**Random intercept.** $y_{tk}=\beta_0+\beta_{d(t)}+b_t+\epsilon_{tk}$, $b_t\sim N(0,\sigma^2_b)$, $\epsilon_{tk}\sim N(0,\sigma^2_\epsilon)$ (tank $t$, fish $k$).

**Variance of a group mean.** $m$ tanks with $n$ fish: $\text{var}[\bar y_d]=\dfrac{\sigma^2_b}{m}+\dfrac{\sigma^2_\epsilon}{mn}$.

**Induced correlation (ICC).** $\text{cov}[y_{tk},y_{tk'}]=\sigma^2_b$; $\text{corr}[y_{tk},y_{tk'}]=\dfrac{\sigma^2_b}{\sigma^2_b+\sigma^2_\epsilon}$.

**Random intercept and slope.** $y_{ij}=(\beta_0+b_{0i})+(\beta_1+b_{1i})\text{week}_j+\epsilon_{ij}$, $(b_{0i},b_{1i})^T\sim N(\mathbf 0,\mathbf D)$; $\text{cov}[y_{ij},y_{ij'}]=\sigma^2_{b_0}+\sigma_{b_0b_1}(\text{week}_j+\text{week}_{j'})+\sigma^2_{b_1}\text{week}_j\text{week}_{j'}+\sigma^2_\epsilon\delta_{jj'}$.

**General LMM.** $\mathbf y=\mathbf X\boldsymbol\beta+\mathbf Z\mathbf b+\boldsymbol\epsilon$, $\mathbf b\sim N(\mathbf 0,\mathbf G)$, $\boldsymbol\epsilon\sim N(\mathbf 0,\mathbf R)$; marginally $\mathbf y\sim N(\mathbf X\boldsymbol\beta,\mathbf V)$, $\mathbf V=\mathbf Z\mathbf G\mathbf Z^T+\mathbf R$.

**Likelihood.** $\ell(\boldsymbol\beta,\mathbf G,\mathbf R)=-\frac n2\log(2\pi)-\frac12\log|\mathbf V|-\frac12(\mathbf y-\mathbf X\boldsymbol\beta)^T\mathbf V^{-1}(\mathbf y-\mathbf X\boldsymbol\beta)$. REML: $\ell_R=\ell(\hat{\boldsymbol\beta},\mathbf G,\mathbf R)-\frac12\log|\mathbf X^T\mathbf V^{-1}\mathbf X|$ (corrects the variance components for the estimation of $\boldsymbol\beta$).

**Best prediction (BLUP).** $E[v\mid y]=E[v]+\dfrac{\text{cov}[v,y]}{\text{var}[y]}(y-E[y])$. Tank effect: $\tilde b_t=\dfrac{n\sigma^2_b}{\sigma^2_\epsilon+n\sigma^2_b}(\bar y_{t\cdot}-\beta_0-\beta_{d(t)})$: shrinkage towards 0. In general $\tilde{\mathbf b}=(\mathbf Z^T\mathbf Z+\sigma^2_\epsilon\mathbf G^{-1})^{-1}\mathbf Z^T(\mathbf y-\mathbf X\tilde{\boldsymbol\beta})$ (for $\mathbf R=\sigma^2_\epsilon\mathbf I$).

**Peptide-level model.** $y_{ip}=\beta_0+\mathbf x_i\boldsymbol\beta^\text{design}+\beta^\text{peptide}_p+b^\text{run}_i+\epsilon_{ip}$: the random run (sample) effect accounts for the correlation between the peptides of the same sample.

**TMT.** $y_{rl}=\mathbf x^T_{rl}\boldsymbol\beta+b^\text{label}_l+b^\text{run}_r+\epsilon_{rl}$; with technical replication of mixtures and samples: $y_{rlm}=\mathbf x^T_{rlm}\boldsymbol\beta+b^\text{label}_l+b^\text{run}_r+b^\text{mix}_m+b^\text{sample}_{ml}+\epsilon_{rlm}$.

# II. Bulk RNA-seq

**Abundance metrics.** $\text{CPM}_{gi}=\dfrac{Y_{gi}}{N_i}10^6$; effective length $l^\text{eff}_{gi}=l_g-\hat{\bar F}_i+1$; $\text{TPM}_{gi}=\dfrac{Y_{gi}/l^\text{eff}_{gi}}{\sum_{g'}Y_{g'i}/l^\text{eff}_{g'i}}10^6$.

**Technical replicates.** $Y_{gr}\sim\text{Poisson}(\mu_g)$: $E[Y]=\text{Var}[Y]=\mu_g$.

**Poisson GLM with offset.** $\log\mu_{gi}=\mathbf x_i^T\boldsymbol\beta_g+\log N_i\Leftrightarrow\log\frac{\mu_{gi}}{N_i}=\mathbf x_i^T\boldsymbol\beta_g$: the parameters describe relative abundances.

**Negative binomial.** $Y_{gi}\sim NB(\mu_{gi},\phi_g)$, $\text{Var}[Y_{gi}]=\mu_{gi}+\phi_g\mu_{gi}^2$; $\sqrt{\phi_g}$ = biological coefficient of variation.

**edgeR quasi-likelihood model.** $\log\mu_{gi}=\mathbf x_i^T\boldsymbol\beta_g+\log N^\text{eff}_i$, $\text{Var}[Y_{gi}]=\sigma_g^2(\mu_{gi}+\phi\mu_{gi}^2)$, $N^\text{eff}_i$ = effective library size (library size $\times$ normalisation factor).

**Interaction.** $\log\mu_{gi}=\beta_{g0}+\ldots+\beta_{g,A}x_{iA}+\beta_{g,B}x_{iB}+\beta_{g,A:B}x_{iA}x_{iB}+\log N^\text{eff}_i$; $\beta_{g,A:B}=\log FC$ of B in level A of the first factor $-\log FC$ of B in the reference level ($\log_2$ scale on the plots).

# II. GLMs and edgeR

**Exponential family.** $f(y_i\mid\theta_i,\phi)=\exp\left\{\frac{y_i\theta_i-b(\theta_i)}{a(\phi)}+c(y_i,\phi)\right\}$; Poisson: $\theta_i=\log\mu_i$, $b(\theta)=e^\theta$, $a(\phi)=1$.

**GLM.** $y_i\mid\mathbf x_i\sim f(y_i\mid\theta_i,\phi)$, $E[y_i\mid\mathbf x_i]=\mu_i$, $g(\mu_i)=\eta_i=\mathbf x_i^T\boldsymbol\beta$; canonical link $\theta_i=\eta_i$ (log for Poisson).

**Poisson log-likelihood.** $l(\boldsymbol\beta\mid\mathbf y)=\sum_i\{y_i\eta_i-e^{\eta_i}-\log y_i!\}$; score $S(\boldsymbol\beta)=\partial l/\partial\boldsymbol\beta=\mathbf X^T(\mathbf y-\boldsymbol\mu)=\mathbf 0$ (canonical link; in general $\mathbf X^T\mathbf A(\mathbf y-\boldsymbol\mu)$).

**IRLS.** $\boldsymbol\beta^{k+1}=(\mathbf X^T\mathbf W\mathbf X)^{-1}\mathbf X^T\mathbf W\mathbf z$ with working response $z_i=\eta_i+\frac{\partial\eta_i}{\partial\mu_i}(y_i-\mu_i)$ and weights $w_{ii}=\text{var}^{-1}_{y_i}\left(\frac{\partial\mu_i}{\partial\eta_i}\right)^2$; Poisson: $z_i=\eta_i+e^{-\eta_i}y_i-1$, $w_{ii}=e^{\eta_i}$.

**Variance and Wald test.** $\hat{\boldsymbol\beta}\stackrel a\sim N[\boldsymbol\beta,(\mathbf X^T\mathbf W\mathbf X)^{-1}]$; $z=\dfrac{\mathbf L^T\hat{\boldsymbol\beta}}{\sqrt{\mathbf L^T\hat{\boldsymbol\Sigma}_{\hat{\boldsymbol\beta}}\mathbf L}}\stackrel a\sim N(0,1)$; $c$ contrasts: $W=(\mathbf L^T\hat{\boldsymbol\beta})^T(\mathbf L^T\hat{\boldsymbol\Sigma}_{\hat{\boldsymbol\beta}}\mathbf L)^{-1}(\mathbf L^T\hat{\boldsymbol\beta})\stackrel a\sim\chi^2_c$.

**Deviance.** $D=2[l(\mathbf y\mid\mathbf y)-l(\hat{\boldsymbol\mu}\mid\mathbf y)]$; Poisson: $D=2\sum_i\left[y_i\log\frac{y_i}{\hat\mu_i}-(y_i-\hat\mu_i)\right]$ ($y\log y\to0$ for $y\to0$).

**Likelihood ratio test.** $\text{LRT}=2[l(\hat{\boldsymbol\beta}_\text{full})-l(\hat{\boldsymbol\beta}_0)]=D_0-D_\text{full}\stackrel d\to\chi^2_c$ under $H_0$.

**Quasi-likelihood.** $E[Y_i]=\mu_i$, $g(\mu_i)=\mathbf x_i^T\boldsymbol\beta$, $\text{Var}[Y_i]=\sigma^2V(\mu_i)$; estimating equations $\mathbf X^T\mathbf A(\mathbf y-\boldsymbol\mu)=\mathbf 0$; $\hat\sigma^2=\dfrac{D}{n-p}$.

**edgeR QL pipeline.** Empirical Bayes: $\tilde\sigma^2_g=\dfrac{d_0s_0^2+d_g\hat\sigma^2_g}{d_0+d_g}$; moderated F-test $F_g=\dfrac{(D_{0,g}-D_{\text{full},g})/c}{\tilde\sigma^2_g}\stackrel a\sim F_{c,d_0+d_g}$ under $H_0$.

**TMM.** $M_{gi}=\log_2\dfrac{Y_{gi}/N_i}{Y_{gr}/N_r}$ w.r.t. reference sample $r$; trimmed weighted mean over the genes $G^*$ after trimming on $M$ and on the average abundance: $\log_2F_i=\dfrac{\sum_{g\in G^*}w_{gi}M_{gi}}{\sum_{g\in G^*}w_{gi}}$, $w_{gi}=\left(\frac{N_i-Y_{gi}}{N_iY_{gi}}+\frac{N_r-Y_{gr}}{N_rY_{gr}}\right)^{-1}$; $N^\text{eff}_i=F_iN_i$.

**Median of ratios (DESeq2).** $s_i=\text{median}_{g:Y^*_g>0}\dfrac{Y_{gi}}{Y^*_g}$, $Y^*_g=\sqrt[n]{\prod_iY_{gi}}$.

**Independent filtering.** The filter must be independent of the test statistic under $H_0$ (e.g. the overall mean, not the variance and not the group labels). `filterByExpr`: CPM $\ge10/\text{median}(N^\text{eff})\times10^6$ in at least $\min_i 1/h_{ii}$ samples (= smallest group size in a one-way design).

**Quantification uncertainty.** Transcript counts are overdispersed: $\text{Var}(Y_{ti})\approx c_t\mu_{ti}$; scaled counts $\tilde Y_{ti}=Y_{ti}/c_t$ restore $\text{Var}(\tilde Y_{ti})=E[\tilde Y_{ti}]$.

**Differential transcript usage.** Usage $\pi_{gti}=\dfrac{E[Y_{gti}]}{E[Y_{g.i}]}$, $Y_{g.i}=\sum_tY_{gti}$; offset $\log Y_{g.i}$ gives $\log\pi_{gti}=\mathbf x_i^T\boldsymbol\beta_{gt}$; with scaled counts the offset becomes $\log Y_{g.i}-\log c_t$.

**Stage-wise testing.** Screening: omnibus test per gene, BH on the screening p-values of all $G$ genes at level $\alpha$; $R$ genes pass. Confirmation: test the individual hypotheses of these genes with FWER control (e.g. Holm, Shaffer) at $\alpha_{II}=R\alpha/G$. Controls the overall FDR (OFDR) at the gene level.

# II. Single-cell RNA-seq

**QC with adaptive thresholds.** Remove cell $i$ if $\log N_i<\text{median}(\log\mathbf N)-3\times\text{MAD}(\log\mathbf N)$ (similar for the number of detected genes; upper threshold for the mitochondrial proportion).

**Count model.** $y_{gi}\sim NB(\mu_{gi},\phi_g)$, $\mu_{gi}=s_iN_i\pi_{gi}$; UMI counts of a homogeneous population are close to Poisson.

**Zero inflation?** ZINB: $f(y_{gi})=\pi^0_{gi}\delta_0(y_{gi})+(1-\pi^0_{gi})f_{NB}(y_{gi};\mu_{gi},\phi_g)$. Common relative abundance: $\hat\pi_g=\sum_iy_{gi}/\sum_iN_i$ (ML under Poisson), $\hat\mu_{gi}=N_i\hat\pi_g$. Expected fraction of zeros: Poisson $\frac1n\sum_ie^{-\hat\mu_{gi}}$; NB $\frac1n\sum_i(1+\phi_g\hat\mu_{gi})^{-1/\phi_g}$. Detection probability (Poisson): $1-e^{-\mu}$.

**Log-normalised counts.** $z_{gi}=\log_2\left(\frac{y_{gi}}{s_i}+1\right)$, $s_i$ size factor centred at one.

**Feature selection: deviance.** Null model $\mu_{gi}=N_i\pi_g$: $D_g=2\sum_i\left[y_{gi}\log\frac{y_{gi}}{\hat\mu_{gi}}-(y_{gi}-\hat\mu_{gi})\right]=2\sum_{i:y_{gi}>0}y_{gi}\log\frac{y_{gi}}{N_i\hat\pi_g}$.

**Pearson residuals.** $r_{gi}=\dfrac{y_{gi}-\hat\mu_{gi}}{\sqrt{\hat\mu_{gi}+\phi\hat\mu_{gi}^2}}$; informative genes: large $\sum_ir_{gi}^2/(n-1)$.

**Generalised matrix factorisation.** $y_{gi}\sim\text{Poisson}(\mu_{gi})$ or $NB(\mu_{gi},\phi)$, $\log\mu_{gi}=\mathbf x_i^T\boldsymbol\beta_g+\boldsymbol\alpha_i^T\mathbf z_g+\mathbf u_i^T\mathbf v_g$: cell covariates $\mathbf x_i$ (default: gene intercept), gene covariates $\mathbf z_g$ (default: cell intercept $\alpha_i$, absorbs the library size), latent factors $\mathbf u_i$ and loadings $\mathbf v_g$.

**Marker genes.** Cohen's $d=\dfrac{\bar z_A-\bar z_B}{s_p}$ (t-statistic without the sample size: $t=d/\sqrt{1/n_A+1/n_B}$); $\text{AUC}=P(z_A>z_B)+\frac12P(z_A=z_B)=\dfrac{U}{n_An_B}$ (Wilcoxon--Mann--Whitney).

**Agreement with labels.** Purity: fraction of cells that belong to the most frequent label of their cluster; adjusted Rand index: agreement between two partitions, corrected for chance (1 perfect, 0 random).

**Pseudobulk DE.** Sum the counts per cell type and sample; $\log\mu_{gpc}=\beta_{g0}+\beta_{g,p}+\beta_{g,\text{stim}}x_c+\log(s_{pc}N_{pc})$ (patient $p$, condition $c$), edgeR QL pipeline. The sample, not the cell, is the experimental unit.

**Differential detection.** $Z_{gs}$ = number of cells of sample $s$ in which gene $g$ is detected, out of $n_s$; $\log\text{E}[Z_{gs}]=\mathbf x_s^T\boldsymbol\beta_g+\log(n_s\,\text{CDR}_s)$, $\text{CDR}_s$ = average detection fraction of the sample; genes with median detection fraction $\ge0.9$ removed; QL test with `poisson.bound = FALSE`.

**Combining DE and DD.** Screening with the harmonic mean $p_g=2/(1/p_g^{DE}+1/p_g^{DD})$, followed by stage-wise testing.

**Differential abundance.** Number of cells per cell type and sample, NB GLM with the total number of cells of the sample as library size: models proportions (compositional).
